name: Doximity Scribe vs Nabla
title: Doximity Scribe vs Nabla: AI Medical Scribe Comparison
description: Compare Doximity Scribe and Nabla AI scribes for clinicians. See differences in pricing, multilingual support, EHR integration, and privacy.

summary.bottom_line: Doximity Scribe is free for US clinicians with copy-paste workflow. Nabla offers 35+ language support, zero server-side data storage, and deep EHR integrations but requires enterprise pricing. Choose Doximity Scribe for free US-only use; choose Nabla for multilingual practices, international use, or native EHR integration.

sections.heading: Doximity Scribe vs Nabla: Overview
sections.content: Doximity Scribe and Nabla represent different approaches to AI medical documentation. Doximity Scribe is free for the 3M+ verified US clinicians on the Doximity network, offering ambient documentation with a simple copy-paste workflow. Nabla is a global platform supporting 35+ languages with deep EHR integrations and a unique privacy model where patient data never touches Nabla's servers (exists only in the clinician's browser). Nabla is ideal for international and multilingual practices; Doximity Scribe is unbeatable for US clinicians on a budget.

sections.heading: Pricing Comparison
sections.content: Doximity Scribe is completely free for qualified US clinicians—the most affordable option for those who qualify. Nabla requires payment: historically ~$119/month for individuals, $299-399/provider/month for enterprise. Nabla no longer publishes public pricing and requires a sales conversation. The free vs. paid difference is significant, but Nabla's multilingual support and EHR integrations may justify the cost for practices serving diverse patient populations.

sections.heading: Feature Differences
sections.content: Nabla's key differentiators are 35+ language support (including Arabic, Mandarin, Spanish, Vietnamese), 20+ native EHR integrations via SMART on FHIR, ICD-10 coding suggestions, and a unique privacy model where data never leaves the clinician's browser. Doximity Scribe's advantages are zero cost, integration with the Doximity ecosystem (Doximity Ask for refinement, Doximity Dialer), and simplicity. Doximity is English-only with copy-paste workflow; Nabla is truly multilingual with deep integrations.

sections.heading: Which Should You Choose?
sections.content: Choose based on your language needs and budget:

recommendations.when: You're a US clinician, see primarily English-speaking patients, are comfortable with copy-paste, or want zero documentation costs
You serve multilingual patient populations, need native EHR integration with Epic/Cerner/athena, practice outside the US, or prioritize zero server-side data storage
You're part of a health organization wanting enterprise-grade deployment with GDPR compliance and deep EHR embedding via Nabla Connect

faqs.q: Can Doximity Scribe work in Spanish?
faqs.a: Doximity Scribe is primarily English-focused and does not advertise multilingual support. Nabla supports 35+ languages including Spanish, making it the better choice for practices serving Spanish-speaking patients.

Nabla has a unique privacy model where audio, transcripts, and notes exist only in the clinician's browser and are never stored on Nabla's servers. Doximity also doesn't store audio (immediately discarded), but data is processed through their servers.

faqs.q: Can international clinicians use Doximity Scribe?
faqs.a: No, Doximity Scribe requires US verification (physicians, NPs, PAs, medical students). International clinicians must use alternatives like Nabla, Freed, or other global AI scribes.
Nabla has native Epic integration with embedded workflow capabilities. Doximity Scribe works with Epic but only via copy-paste. For deep Epic integration, Nabla is the clear winner.
